text: It was now fully night, and a thick, humid fog that had hung over the city soon ended in a settled and heavy rain, so I tied a handkerchief about my mouth and kept on. <break time="0.8s" /> For half an hour the old man held his way with difficulty along the great thoroughfare, and though I walked close at his elbow, he never once turned round to look at me. <break time="0.8s" /> Turning into a side street that was less crowded, he walked more slowly and with less object than before, crossing and recrossing the way without any apparent aim. <break time="0.8s" /> At length he entered a square, brilliantly lighted and overflowing with life, where he walked round and round for another hour, his chin sunk upon his breast and his eyes rolling wildly over the faces around him. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he hurried into a vast bazaar, where he passed from shop to shop, priced nothing, spoke no word, and looked at all the objects with a wild and vacant stare. <break time="0.8s" /> When a loud toned clock struck eleven, a shopkeeper, while putting up a shutter, jostled the old man, and at that instant a strong shudder ran through his whole frame. <break time="0.8s" /> Rushing through a maze of crooked lanes, he reached one of the principal theatres just as it was closing, and plunged eagerly into the audience as they poured out through the doors. <break time="0.8s" /> He seemed to gasp for breath as he threw himself amid the crowd, but the intense agony of his countenance had, I thought, in some measure abated, as if the crowd itself gave him relief.
